articles.summary: Bank Rakyat's corporate and login web pages were defaced on the night of 6 November, and the bank took most sites offline. The communications minister said the defacement hit a third-party-hosted site, with no data theft or disruption to core banking. The prime minister ordered a security review of government assets, banks and GLCs.
articles.title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack

articles.summary: An intruder reached a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one Health Ministry facility on 12 November. The ministry's response team found no encryption of main databases and no disruption to treatment. Access was blocked, passwords reset and MFA enforced, with NACSA involved under the Cyber Security Act 2024.
articles.title: Health Ministry reports cyber breach at facility, services unaffected

articles.summary: Malaysia Airlines said its own systems were not compromised, but reservation provider Amadeus told it that customer data processed between August 2023 and September 2026 was involved. The airline has not stated how many people were affected and says it has no evidence financial data was accessed.
articles.title: Malaysia Airlines' systems untouched by data breach

articles.summary: NACSA lifted the National Cyber Threat Level from Low to Medium on 4 November as a precaution after recent security developments. It later said the level stays at Medium with no sudden rise in incidents, while critical sectors must send weekly threat status reports.
articles.title: Nacsa raises level of cyber security threat to medium

articles.summary: On 10 November NACSA warned that attackers increasingly aim at operational technology controlling water, energy and healthcare. It urged operators of critical infrastructure to isolate critical operating systems from external networks and strengthen service continuity plans. Critical sector heads must also send weekly threat reports to NACSA, which has urged the public not to spread unverified claims.
articles.title: NACSA warns cybercriminals increasingly target OT that runs water, energy and healthcare

articles.summary: Minister Fahmi Fadzil said no major cyber threat had been reported so far, including against government systems, as NACSA kept the national level at Medium. He named AI-agent swarm attacks among the most worrying risks and said NACSA would act if they approached Malaysia.
articles.title: Tiada laporan ancaman siber besar setakat ini - Fahmi

articles.summary: The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted cyberattack that disrupted several of its services, which it took offline to contain the incident. It reports no data breach so far and has not attributed the attack to any known group.
articles.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattack Disrupted Services

articles.summary: N-able said unknown actors accessed a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud, after a disruption that began 16 November. Mail filtering continued, but portals, APIs and quarantine stayed offline across Americas, APAC and Europe. It has found no evidence of customer data compromise.
articles.title: N-able confirms hackers accessed Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server

articles.region: Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore & South Korea
articles.summary: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines, Korean Air and Asiana reported passenger booking data exposed through Amadeus, whose account credentials the attackers used. Cathay cited 53,000 bookings and JAL about 92,000 customers; payment data was reportedly not accessed.
articles.title: Asian airlines announce data breaches after IT provider incident

articles.summary: Chase said an attack on a third-party provider exposed customer names and email addresses. Mastercard said only a small subset of cardholder emails was involved. The data was linked to a compromise of Qubole and was leaked by an extortion group on 16 November.
articles.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info

articles.summary: Equinor said it was dealing with a cyberattack against its systems but that gas and oil production continued normally. The company has not published details of the intrusion or its impact on operational technology, and the investigation is still under way.
articles.title: Norwegian Gas Giant Equinor Says It's Under Cyberattack. Production Keeps Running

articles.summary: Maersk confirmed a data breach at a company it had previously acquired, while the WhiteArmor ransomware group demanded 5 million dollars. The shipping giant says its investigation continues and has not stated how much data was taken or whether customer information was involved.
articles.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million

articles.summary: Declassified minutes of the 18 September Federal Territories Pardons Board show the minister first resisted signing Najib's conditional pardon, citing political implications, before the Agong decided she should sign. Najib began house arrest on 10 November and the leak has triggered a row within government.
articles.title: Hannah wanted another officer to sign Najib's pardon, minutes show

articles.summary: After the Home Minister proposed releasing the Pardons Board minutes, Cabinet on 13 November asked the Attorney-General for advice instead of deciding. The matter intensified after minutes appeared online days later, with Umno MPs demanding clarity on their authenticity and status.
articles.title: Cabinet seeks AG's advice on proposal to declassify Najib's pardon board minutes, says Fahmi

milestones.label: Seremban High Court contempt hearing, Negeri Sembilan royal dispute
Federal Court hearing on sacked Negeri Sembilan excos constitutional challenge

articles.summary: The Seremban High Court ordered the disputed undangs and other nobles to attend contempt hearings in person, setting 15 December, as the royal dispute continues. The Court of Appeal recently refused stays, and the Federal Court is to hear a related challenge by sacked state executive councillors on 16 December.
articles.title: Disputed Undang, others ordered to attend contempt hearings in Negri Sembilan royal dispute

milestones.label: Budget 2027 committee-stage debate scheduled to end
Dewan Rakyat sitting scheduled to end

articles.summary: The Dewan Rakyat passed the Budget 2027 Supply Bill at policy stage on 29 October by voice vote. Committee-stage debates run to 26 November, followed by a third reading, Dewan Negara approval and royal assent. The sitting ends on 8 December.
articles.title: Dewan Rakyat passes Budget 2027 at policy stage

articles.summary: The Finance Bill 2026 and the Tax Collection, Administration and Enforcement Measures Bill 2026 were tabled for first reading on 16 November. Both are due for second reading in the current sitting, and the second bill would carry additional government expenditure not yet quantified.
articles.title: Finance Ministry tables two bills on Monday

articles.summary: The Election Commission fixed polling for the 13th Sarawak state election on 12 December, with nomination on 28 November and early voting on 8 December. About 2.05 million voters will elect 82 assemblymen over a 14-day campaign that ends on 11 December, using 97 nomination centres.
articles.title: Sarawak polls set for Dec 12

articles.summary: MACC arrested a man in his fifties on 17 November over alleged bribes to enforcement officers, then handed him to the Chinese Embassy on 19 November after finding he was wanted in China with a revoked passport. No Malaysian charge has been reported.
articles.title: Wanted in China, detained in Putrajaya: MACC hands man over to embassy

articles.summary: Anthony Loke resigned as Transport Minister with immediate effect on 11 November. Government spokesman Fahmi said the resignation was not discussed in Cabinet on 13 November and that the prime minister would meet Loke soon. No successor had been named in the reports reviewed.
articles.title: Loke resigns as Transport Minister with immediate effect

articles.fixedIn: Fixed in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; vCenter 7.0 has no public patch and no workaround exists.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123890

response.text: Triggered by the CVE, it lists vCenter assets from the CMDB or va_endpoints-covered hosts and compares builds with the fixed versions. It opens one ticket per unpatched vCenter and gathers recent SSO administrator creation events from logs. Patching and any credential rotation need analyst approval.
response.title: vCenter exposure and compromise hunt

response.text: A script queries vCenter audit logs ingested in XSIAM for new SSO administrator accounts and unexpected access to port 2012 since 1 September. It returns a table of suspicious entries for the analyst. It is read-only so it can run without approval.
response.title: Check vCenter SSO account changes

response.prompt: Summarise the activity on vCenter host {host} since 2026-09-01 related to CVE-2026-123890: new SSO administrator accounts, access to TCP 2012, unusual SAML or LMDB file access. List the evidence, confidence and next containment steps for analyst approval.
response.text: This asks the Cortex AI assistant to condense the incident evidence for hand-off. Review output before acting.
response.title: Summarise vCenter compromise indicators

response.text: Use XSIAM Vulnerability and Exposure Management to see which vCenter assets are affected and track remediation, instead of building a custom tracker. Pair it with a firewall rule that limits management access to admin networks until patched.
response.title: Use Emerging Vulnerabilities view

articles.summary: An unauthenticated network attacker can bypass vCenter authentication through the Directory Service and gain administrator access. Google attributes zero-day use since early September to a suspected China-nexus group. Broadcom patched on 19 November, and CISA added it to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade clustered Expressway to X15.5.20 or later; X14 and earlier have no fix and should migrate; Cisco lists no workaround.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466

response.text: A scheduled job pulls Expressway software versions through the configured integration or inventory and flags clustered units below X15.5.20. It posts a ranked list to the vulnerability ticket queue. Remediation scheduling stays with the network team.
response.title: Scheduled Expressway version audit

response.text: For each exposed unit, the playbook queries XSIAM for outbound connections from Expressway hosts and new admin or root sessions since 5 November. It enriches destination IPs and attaches findings to the incident. Isolation or credential reset requires analyst approval.
response.title: Expressway compromise triage

response.prompt: Draft a change request to upgrade Cisco Expressway clusters to X15.5.20 for CVE-2026-76466 (hard-coded credentials, root RCE, exploited, public PoC). Include affected hosts {hosts}, rollback plan, interim network restrictions on cluster database ports, and the compromise-check evidence required beforehand.
response.text: This helps the team prepare the upgrade request and risk summary quickly. Review the draft before submission.
response.title: Draft Expressway change request

response.text: Until upgrades finish, an NGFW rule limiting cluster database traffic to peer nodes removes most remote exposure. It is faster than writing automation and is easy to reverse.
response.title: Restrict cluster ports at firewall

articles.summary: Clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E devices contain hard-coded credentials that give an unauthenticated attacker root command execution. Cisco patched in October and a public exploit appeared on 5 November. F6 reported a real intrusion on 19 November, and CISA listed the flaw on 20 November.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later; otherwise set enabledForExtensions to false in web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping and restart.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448

response.text: An automation searches the asset inventory and XSIAM web logs for hosts serving Roller or requests to the roller-services XML-RPC path. It returns a list of candidate servers and request counts for each. It makes no changes.
response.title: Find Roller instances

response.text: Block the roller-services XML-RPC path at the WAF or reverse proxy now, since disabling XML-RPC in the admin console does not stop the deserialization. This is quicker and safer than scripting server edits across hosts.
response.title: WAF block on XML-RPC path

response.text: For any exposed instance, the playbook collects web-server logs, process creation events from XSIAM agents and outbound connections, then opens an incident with the evidence. Containment such as isolating the host needs analyst approval.
response.title: Roller exploitation response

response.prompt: Review these web server log lines for host {host}: identify POST requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc with unusual payload sizes or Java serialization markers, list source IPs and timestamps after 2026-11-10, and say whether exploitation of CVE-2026-129448 is likely.
response.text: This prompt speeds up reviewing noisy web logs. Verify findings in the raw logs.
response.title: Roller log triage helper

articles.summary: Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 to 6.1.4 deserialize XML-RPC requests before authentication, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Maintainers said the flaw is being actively exploited and a public proof of concept exists. CISA added it to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline.

timeline.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required

articles.fixedIn: Install the Check Point Jumbo Hotfix take listed in advisory sk1000362 for the affected Gaia release (R81.20, R82, R82.10, R82.20).

response.text: The playbook lists Check Point gateways and management servers, reads installed Jumbo Hotfix takes and flags those below the advisory minimum. It creates tickets per gateway with the owner and current take. Patch scheduling stays with the firewall team.
response.title: Gaia hotfix compliance check

response.text: An automation pulls gateway audit logs from XSIAM for new shells, unexpected root processes or writes to the local socket path since 1 November. It outputs flagged gateways for review. It is read-only.
response.title: Review Gaia admin sessions

response.text: Limit Mobile Access portal exposure by source and disable it where unused, which blocks the reported initial access path while hotfixes roll out. This reduces risk faster than building new detections.
response.title: Restrict Mobile Access portal

response.prompt: Summarise suspicious activity on Check Point gateway {gw} since 2026-11-01 relevant to CVE-2026-123039: web shell indicators on Mobile Access, new root shells, DynamicCLI socket access. List evidence, confidence and recommended next steps requiring approval.
response.text: This summarises gateway evidence for the shift handover. Confirm results against the original logs.
response.title: Gateway forensic summary

articles.summary: A local privilege escalation in Check Point Gaia lets an attacker with a foothold reach root. Reports say attackers combined it with a Mobile Access portal flaw for initial access. CISA added it to KEV on 13 November with a 16 November deadline, so the federal deadline has passed.
